raw_response:
Eight useful references emerged from the searches. A user namespace plus coordinated UID/GID allocation is the closest fit; applying container-level mechanisms to a shared pod boundary is a design inference that still needs lifecycle and storage integration.

1. [Linux user namespaces](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/user_namespaces.7.html) supply the core mapping from internal root to an unprivileged host identity and scope capabilities to namespace-owned resources. Create associated resource namespaces under the intended user namespace; this permission boundary cannot guarantee protection from every kernel flaw. Evidence timing: the opened manual is dated 2026-02-08, after the cutoff.

2. [OCI runtime-spec user-namespace configuration](https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/blob/main/config-linux.md) supplies UID/GID range fields and namespace-path joining that could transmit one pod allocation to its containers. Allocation policy and filesystem ownership handling remain additional work. Evidence timing: unknown for the retrieved live body; the separately verified 2020 v1.0.2 release date cannot backdate it.

3. [LXD isolated identity maps](https://stgraber.org/2017/06/15/custom-user-mappings-in-lxd-containers/) demonstrate separate nonoverlapping UID/GID blocks per container, adaptable to per-pod assignment. The documented constraints are subordinate-ID capacity, filesystem remapping cost, and difficulty sharing storage between distinct maps. Evidence timing: original post dated 2017-06-15.

4. [Podman v4.3 auto user namespaces](https://docs.podman.io/en/v4.3/markdown/podman-create.1.html) demonstrate unique range allocation, estimated or explicit range sizing, and joining an existing container namespace. Adapt container allocation lifetime to pod lifetime and provision the subordinate-ID pools. Evidence timing: the versioned manual is supported by the official archive's 2022-10-22 v4.3.0 release entry.

5. [Docker userns-remap](https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/userns-remap/) demonstrates workload UID/GID remapping while its daemon remains root, matching the boundary that runtime rootlessness is outside this decision. Its daemon-level setup needs a separate pod allocation policy, and bind mounts, host namespace sharing, and fully privileged modes have documented limitations. Evidence timing: unknown for this live documentation.

6. [Linux idmapped mounts](https://docs.kernel.org/filesystems/idmappings.html) could address ownership mismatches when distinct pod identity maps access images or shared volumes, using mount-local translation instead of global ownership rewrites. Filesystem and kernel support plus explicit sharing policy are conditions; this mechanism does not allocate IDs. Evidence timing: unknown for the live page.

7. [runc's libcontainer example](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/blob/main/libcontainer/example_test.go) connects separate UID/GID maps with container creation and an internal UID-zero process. It is useful implementation scaffolding, but its sample host ID must be replaced with a safely reserved allocation. Evidence timing: unknown for current main-branch code.

8. [Firecracker's NSDI 2020 design](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi20/presentation/agache) offers an alternative virtualization boundary if the broader goal requires protection beyond shared-kernel isolation. This is a larger architectural change and does not itself supply host UID/GID allocation; its applicability here is an inference. Evidence timing: primary paper page dates the work to 2020.
